item.title: Why Bodybuilders Collapse Before 40 (5 Silent Organ Traps)
item.description:
Sometimes bodybuilders pass away way too young. The media always blames a "steroid overdose," and buddies at the gym blame "bad heart genetics." Neither are right. Here are the 5 overlooked organ traps that basic doctor blood tests miss, explained in plain English with zero medical jargon.

⚠️ MEDICAL & EDUCATIONAL DISCLAIMER (EDSA): This video is strictly for educational, documentary, scientific, and harm-reduction purposes. I am not a medical doctor. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ⏱️ CHAPTERS: 0:00 The "Steroid Overdose" & "Bad Genetics" Lie 1:30 Trap #1: Sticky Blood Clots & Why Thick Blood Ruins Your Gym Pump 5:10 Trap #2: Hidden Heart Wall Scar Tissue (The 3 AM Short-Circuit) 7:20 Trap #3: The "Zero Calcium Score" Heart Attack Under 45 (Soft Plaque) 9:35 Inside the Thomsen Performance Private Discord Vault 10:05 Trap #4: Nighttime Choking & Sleeping Blood Pressure (Sleep Apnea) 11:30 Trap #5: Kidney Filters, Cystatin-C vs. Creatinine & The Ibuprofen Trap 14:00 The 30-Second Heart Math Check Every Lifter Needs to Run ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
📚 KEY BLOODWORK MARKERS & TESTS DISCUSSED (For Your Doctor): 1. Blood Thickness & Clotting: Hydrated Hematocrit (45-49%), Fibrinogen clotting protein (200-300 mg/dL), Platelets (<325k), D-Dimer (<0.4), Homocysteine (<8), Ferritin (stored iron >30-40), Factor V Leiden genetic test. 2. Heart Wall & Electrical Health: Resting Heart Rate x Systolic Blood Pressure (<7,500), Cardiac MRI with contrast dye + Strain Echocardiogram. 3. Artery Soft Plaque (Under Age 45): ApoB (<60-65 mg/dL), hs-CRP inflammation (<0.6 mg/L), Lp(a) genetic cholesterol check (<30), Dye-Contrast Coronary CT Angiogram (CCTA). 4. Sleep & Nighttime Blood Pressure: Home sleep apnea test, 24-hour blood pressure cuff (checking nighttime drop below 110/65). 5. True Kidney Filtration: Cystatin-C (<0.92 mg/L; not skewed by muscle mass, heavy training, steak, or creatine) + First-Morning Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (uACR <5).
